title: Sorting and copying arrays safely
learningObjectives: Explain sorting and copying arrays safely and process JavaScript collections correctly.

understand.concept: sort() sorts an array in place and converts elements to strings by default for comparison. A compare function provides numeric or custom ordering. To copy before sorting, use slice(), spread syntax, or toSorted() where supported. Shallow copies do not clone nested objects.
understand.whyItMatters: Mutating a shared array can change data unexpectedly elsewhere. Use a copy when a sorted view should not alter the original collection, and understand that nested objects remain shared in shallow copies.
understand.analogy: Sorting rearranges the same row of cards; copying first creates a separate row that can be rearranged independently.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; JavaScript array and object methods have defined mutation, iteration, and reference semantics.

explain.narrative: The original array remains in its original order, while the copied array is sorted numerically.

examples.explanation: The original array remains in its original order, while the copied array is sorted numerically.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser console displays the array or object values described.

practise.guidedTask: Sort an array of numbers ascending and descending without changing the source array. Explain why the compare function is needed.
practise.independentTask: Build a small collection-processing example using arrays and objects. Test empty collections, missing values, and mutation behaviour.
hints: Check whether a method mutates or returns a new value.
Use clear object property names and deliberate copying.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Sorting and copying arrays safely</title></head><body>
<script>const scores=[90,8,40];const sorted=[...scores].sort((a,b)=>a-b);console.log(scores,sorted);</script>
</body></html>

questions.prompt: Why should a compare function be supplied for numeric sorting?
options: Because default sort compares values as strings
questions.answer: Because default sort compares values as strings
questions.explanation: Default sort compares string representations, which can produce unexpected numeric order.

questions.prompt: What should you check when using an array method?
options: Whether it mutates the source or returns a new value
Whether the array contains strings only
questions.answer: Whether it mutates the source or returns a new value
questions.explanation: Mutation behaviour matters when arrays are shared across application code.
